text:
emma_support: Heads up — escalated billing case from ACME. Their Feb invoice shows ~40% fewer tokens for streaming calls vs dashboard. Customer says their client cancels the stream early and suspects tokens after the early chunks weren't billed.

raj_engineer: Do we have request IDs and timestamps? Need a concrete repro. @emma_support can you paste a few rIDs + times.

emma_support: Sent three example IDs: req_7f3a, req_7f3b, req_7f3c (2026-02-14 15:02:11 UTC). Customer logs show client closed SSE after receiving a partial final chunk.

tom_sre: On our side logs show repeated SSE disconnects with reason=client_cancel. Example: [req_7f3a] stream_end reason=client_cancel seq=12 chunk_id=2 remote_addr=10.2.4.8

raj_engineer: My hunch: metering currently only tallies tokens when we see the "final" event. If the client cancels before we emit final, we never increment invoice-facing counters. Dashboard had interim counts (from debug stream) so numbers diverge.

maya_billing: That would explain invoice < dashboard. Invoices are generated from the billing stream which expects a final total per request. If final never arrives, invoice uses 0 or last checkpointed total.

olivia_prodops: Can repro locally with a quick curl + Ctrl+C. Script I used:
```bash
curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-3\" \
  | sed -n '1,20p'
# then hit ctrl+c after chunk 3 to simulate client cancel
```

raj_engineer: Ran similar. Confirmed meter.record() is only called when chunk.end == true. When the client cancels mid-stream we never run the final tally. Proposed fix: estimate tokens on every chunk receipt and emit interim_meter events to the billing queue; on final event reconcile to exact count.

raj_engineer: Opening PR with changes + tests: PR #2468. Changes include: - count tokens for partial chunks on receipt - emit interim_meter events (type=partial) - ensure final event reconciles and marks request closed - add integration test simulating abrupt client disconnects

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for service=streams version=2026.03.17-fix-2468 in prod-small

tom_sre: Canary ran 30m with no perf regressions. Observed interim_meter events flowing to billing queue for active streams. No backpressure issues.

maya_billing: After full rollout we'll run a reconciliation to recompute totals for affected request IDs and issue credits. I created ticket BILL-921 to track credits and ledger adjustments.

emma_support: Notified ACME that engineering identified a metering gap for client-cancel SSE and we're rolling a fix. Offered to issue provisional credit; waiting on their confirmation.

olivia_prodops: Full rollout ETA ~2h. After rollout I'll run reconciliation script: /ops/reconcile/stream_tokens.py --from=2026-02-01 --to=2026-02-28 --ids=req_7f3a,req_7f3b,req_7f3c

maya_billing: Credit issued to ACME: $724.00. Billing note: undercount due to SSE client_cancel edge case; invoice adjusted and memoed under BILL-921.

raj_engineer: Follow-ups: add SDK signal for explicit client-cancel (so clients can send a cancel event and we can emit final tally), add unit+integration tests, and add telemetry that flags requests with client_cancel without final event.

emma_support: :thumbsup: Closing escalation for now — credit issued and fix deployed to prod. I'll file a short KB: KB-streams-metering-client-cancel with repro & mitigation notes.
